notes: Volume D–F of the collection: 56 pages, 35 biographies of architects, builders, engineers, landscape architects, developers and firms whose names begin D, E or F, read end to end — the title page, the three letter indexes, every biography (education, firms, cultural identification, narrative and footnotes), every 'Projects in San Francisco' and 'Other notable projects' list, and every figure caption. The collection is eight PDFs on one landing page (A–C, D–F, G–I, J–L, M–O, P–R, S–U, V–Z) plus a case report and an evaluation framework; this batch is the second volume. There is no inventory table and no APN anywhere in the document, so the record-parcel check that resolve_eas.py's report prints has nothing to test against here. The 'Projects in San Francisco' lists are the dense seam, as in A–C: 31 of the 35 entries carry one, and nearly every line is an address, a year and a building name already attached to a named practitioner. Two entries (Vernon DeMars, Donn Emmons) name only unnumbered civic projects and yielded nothing; a third (Prentiss French) yielded one unnumbered housing project.

coverage.remaining: Volumes G–I, J–L, M–O, P–R, S–U and V–Z of the same collection — six more PDFs from the same landing page, each its own batch. Volumes A–C and D–F are finished.
coverage.note: 260 numbered-address mentions across 56 pages became 208 findings. The gap is deduplication, not sampling: 41 addresses are printed more than once — the same project appears under each partner and again under the firm (2801 Leavenworth Street under Peter Dodge and under Joseph Esherick with different years, 420 Filbert Street and 530 Parnassus Avenue under Dodge and under EHDD, 69 Potomac Street under both Dencks, 296 Addison Street under Jorge de Quesada and under Garrett Eckbo as 296A), the narrative repeats what the list already gave, and almost every biography opens with a figure caption naming an address from its own list. Each project was recorded once, credited to the firm where the volume has a firm entry, with the variant year, street type or unit letter kept in extra. 191 of the 208 reached a parcel and 17 did not: 9 recorded ranges now split across separate parcels (517-532 Greenwich, 315-317 Green, 1501-1515 Grant, 929-931 Market, 1493-1499 McAlister, 2413-2417 Franklin, 142-160 Central, 144-146 Lake, 1963 Clay), 7 numbers the city no longer has (300 34th Avenue, 1750 Scott, 1977 Clay, 351 Filbert, 1933 15th Avenue, 100 32nd Avenue, 1001-1009 McAllister) and 1 street the address register does not hold (1 Maritime Plaza, the same gap volume A–C hit). Of the 191, 138 were published onto 138 pages (104 created by this run, 34 already on the site) and 53 declined: 50 where the page already carried the same credit at the same date from a neighbourhood survey that documented the building first — 35 of them found by a name-and-date scan the overlap tool's wording threshold missed, mostly Henry Doelger's Sunset model homes and the North Beach builders, 2 whose parcel has no 2025 secured-roll row so the seeder will not make a page (3250 18th Street, 115 Red Rock Way), and 1 undated landscaping credit on a Golden Gate Park parcel with no component to carry it. 35 published findings state a disagreement with the assessor: 8 say, unadjudicated, that the building described may not be the one standing, and 27 record a construction-date disagreement. Addresses NOT recorded, and why: places named without a street number (Forest Hill tract, Presidio Park, Treasure Island and the 1939 Exposition, the Brazilian Pavilion on Yerba Buena Island, the de Young remodel and Strybing Arboretum in Golden Gate Park, Red Rock Hill Condominiums at Diamond Heights Boulevard and Duncan Street, the Golden Gateway and Western Addition A-1 and Diamond Heights site plans, the BART consultancy, Hunters View, Tenderloin Community School, the Dogpatch houses given as '1000 block of Tennessee and 900 block of Minnesota'); Henry Doelger's model homes located only by intersection (The Chester at Ortega and 18th Avenue, The Windsor at 31st and Lawton, The Normandie at 18th Avenue and Ortega, The Padre and The Deauville and The Yorkshire at 33rd Avenue and Kirkham, 'W 29th Avenue, 150 S Ortega', the '1800 block of 30th avenue', the development at Orange Avenue and Market Street); projects the volume itself marks 'unknown address' (the Doble landscaping, the California Commission and Federal Building, the Southern Counties Building, the Chinese Village, Saint Thomas Moore Church, the Robinhood and Allen houses, the Ferris Bagley residence, the Legion of Honor and St. Mary's Square landscaping); and every address outside San Francisco. Addresses seen and deliberately not recorded under the people rule, because the only fact attached is where a person lived: 2123 Powell Street (Paul DeMartini), 1069 Vallejo Street (Joseph Devincenzi), 2205 Pine Street (Oliver Everett's childhood home) and 1321 Mason Street (Henry Doelger's birthplace). Twelve building names were dropped at extraction for the same reason, the address, the credit and the year kept: the Berliner, Heil, Roos, Goldman, Babcock, Guggenheim, Heymes and Taravellier houses, the Lilienthal residence, the Bliss Flats, the Alfred G. Hanson House at 126 27th Avenue (San Francisco Landmark No. 196, kept by its landmark number instead) and the Gardner Dailey House at 275 Telegraph Hill Boulevard, kept as a Dailey design without the occupancy.
